title: Gold Plates in Paradise, Despair in Hell

paragraphs.text: On that Day, close friends will become enemies to one another, except for the righteous. Allah will call to His servants, those who believed in His verses and were Muslims, and assure them that there is no fear for them that Day and that they will never grieve. They will be invited to enter Paradise together with their kind, full of joy. Plates and cups of gold will be passed around among them, and they will have whatever their souls desire and whatever pleases their eyes, living there forever. This Paradise is given to them as an inheritance because of their deeds, and in it there is much fruit, more than enough, from which they will eat.

The criminals, however, will remain in the punishment of Hell forever. It will never be eased for them, and they will be in complete despair. This punishment is not unfair, because Allah did not wrong them in any way; rather, it was they who were the wrongdoers. They will call out to Malik, begging that their Lord put an end to them, but he will answer that they will remain there. Allah had certainly brought them the truth, yet most of them disliked the truth and turned from it.

Have the disbelievers decided on some plan against the truth? If so, Allah too is making a plan. Do they think He does not hear their secrets and private talks? He certainly does, and His messengers stay with them, writing everything down. The Prophet is told to say that if the Most Merciful had a son, he would be the first to worship him. But the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Throne, is exalted far above what they describe. So the Prophet should leave them to chatter and play until they meet the Day they have been promised.

to say what something is like
to talk a lot about useless things
